title: 20th sitting of the 19th Majlis
summary: After routine business (agenda, minutes of two earlier sittings accepted, a government bill to amend the Employment Act read for the first time), the House voted 57-0 to debate an urgent matter from Ibrahim Nazil about repeated power cuts in Addu City. About 20 members spoke, with the opposition blaming slow government action and government-side members pointing to past management of the state utility, a damaged cable from road works and capacity limits; the debate time was extended by a 48-0 vote. After a break the House took up the General Committee report on drafting the 20th Majlis rules, and an amendment to the urgent-matter debate time limits was put forward before the vote. This part covers the end of the sitting, when the Majlis finished work on its new Rules of Procedure for the 20th Majlis. Velidhoo MP Mohamed Abbas's amendment (seconded by Inguraidhoo MP Ibrahim Falah) to the General Committee's draft rules passed 63-0, and the full rules including that amendment then passed 64-0. The Speaker thanked the General Committee for its work and adjourned to Monday 29 July 2024 at 9:00. The rest is the electronic voting records for four votes held during the sitting.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Submitted the urgent matter: repeated blackouts in Addu City islands, accusing the government of neglect and calling the energy minister to account.
Said spare parts and engine maintenance were not provided and residents lack power and water.
Raised points of order, including that claims of corruption had not been proven by any court.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the government is working day and night on the outages and moved to let all members who wish to speak on the matter do so.
On the rules report, supported it and called claims that urgent matters become harder to submit untrue.
Backed the proposed amendment and said the majority would not misuse its numbers.
Supported the Velidhoo member's proposal to extend the time allowed for debating an urgent matter under the rules.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Called the urgent matter a political move and said blackouts follow years of wasteful spending at the utility.
Proposed amending the Rules article on urgent matters: one hour of debate, 7 minutes for the proposer, 5 minutes for other members.
Formally submitted the amendment to the rules article at vote time.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: On the urgent matter, said essential services matter to all citizens and blamed past management of the state utility.
As committee rapporteur, presented the General Committee report on the 20th Majlis rules.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Said the problem is nationwide and engines received no preventive maintenance in recent years.
Said those responsible for wrongdoing should face the courts.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Said Addu outages date back years, engines are being replaced, and a new power station is to be built under an agreement signed with a Chinese company.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Attributed the outages to past mismanagement and alleged corruption at the state utility and called for firm action against those responsible.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said Addu faces capacity shortfalls and slow road works, and that Addu was neglected in the past five years.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Thanked Nazil, described days of hardship without power or water, and urged the government to finish the unfinished power station project.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Said the record of the former majority should be examined and that urgent matters displace the House's other work.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Listed past outage dates from 2019 to 2023 and asked what the earlier majority did about them.

speakers.name: Yoosuf Nasheed
positions: Said power problems also affect Laamu atoll islands and are not limited to Addu, and defended the new government's approach.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said the cause is limited capacity and a cable fault during road works, not only spare parts, and referred to a 32 MW project with a Chinese company.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said essential service interruptions hurt residents of every party and called for joint solutions, noting similar cuts in his own area.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Said the issue affects all islands and traced it to the state utility's large debts and supply problems.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Said the Addu cut came from a cable damaged during road construction and pointed to a large project already in its assessment stage.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Thanked the utility's technicians and said load, spare parts and cable networks are the problems; the President has been briefed.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naufal
positions: Said three powerhouses in his constituency are in poor condition and asked for an investigation and for the former utility head to be summoned.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Questioned whether the urgent matter was warranted, said the damaged cable had been repaired, and objected to comparing Addu with Palestine.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Blamed past neglect of engine servicing and misuse of funds, and said the present government will fix the problem.

speakers.name: Mohamed Afoo Hamid
positions: Said many generator sets were unusable when the government took over and that a 31.2 MW power station contract has been awarded.

decisions: Minutes of the 14th and 15th sittings of 2024 accepted by the chair with no amendments submitted.
First reading read for the government bill amending the Employment Act (Law 2/2008).
Urgent matter on Addu City power outages accepted for debate, 57 yes, none against, 60 present.
Debate extended until all members who wished to speak had spoken, 48 yes, none against, 50 present.
General Committee report on the 20th Majlis rules debated; debate closed and vote scheduled; amendment to the urgent-matter debate rule submitted.
Mohamed Abbas's amendment to the draft Rules of Procedure passed.
The Rules of Procedure of the 20th Majlis, with the amendment, were passed and take effect.
The chair thanked the General Committee and its rapporteur for drafting the amendments.
Next sitting set for Monday 29 July 2024 at 9:00.
